## Overview
Mount Giligaon is a mountain located in Siaton, Negros Oriental, in the Central Visayas region of the Philippines. With an elevation of 731 meters (2,398 feet) above sea level and a prominence of 71 meters, it ranks 9th out of 17 mountains in Negros Oriental and 2nd out of 3 mountains in the Siaton municipality.

## Location and Geography
Mount Giligaon is situated at coordinates 9°7'42"N 122°57'49"E. The nearest higher peak is Mount Malbag (782m elevation), located 1.4 km to the east-southeast. The mountain is part of the Bonbonon range that sweeps dramatically from distant mountains through rolling terrain to Siaton's lengthy shoreline.

## Nearby Attractions
The Giligaon area is known for its enchanting waterfalls. Giligaon Falls is a popular destination tucked into Siaton's interiors. The trek to the falls involves passing through farms, crossing gentle streams, and navigating over gigantic boulders. After more than an hour of trekking and bouldering, visitors are rewarded with the amazing cascades. The main cascade is located further inward, requiring climbs over steep rocks to reach.

## Hiking in the Area
While Mount Giligaon itself has limited documented hiking trails, the surrounding Siaton area offers excellent hiking opportunities. Horseshoe Peak, located above the nearby Lake Balanan, is a popular hike starting from 215m altitude and finishing at 610m over a 3.6km trail. The hike offers great views over the southern half of Negros Oriental and Lake Balanan.

## Lake Balanan
Near Mount Giligaon lies Lake Balanan, a freshwater figure-8 shaped lake found deep in the mountains of Barangay Sandulot. The lake is bounded by mountain ranges and fed by three streams. Activities include fishing, kayaking, boat riding, and hiking along cemented pathways to enjoy magnificent views and fresh mountain breezes.

## How to Get There
From Dumaguete City, Siaton is approximately 50 kilometers away. Take a Siaton-bound Ceres Bus from the main bus terminal. To reach Giligaon, alight at Giligaon Market and hire a local guide for trekking. Alternatively, from the Siaton bus terminal, hire a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) to Barangay Giliga-on.
